Let n_i(a) be training predecessor counts by current region and P_ab be the frozen-count, current-region transition matrix; D_ik=sum_a normalize(n_i)_a P_ak. Then a_i=argmax_k[-d_{-1}(z_i,v_k)^2/T+lambda(A_i dot g_k)+eps D_ik]. If no predecessor exists, set D_ik=0. Update the RQ-VAE using these assignments and its ordinary objective.

specification.text: Let A be the symmetric cosine matrix of train-only co-consumption rows, z_i=exp_0^(-1)(encoder(x_i)) (with the implementation convention that exp_0 maps tangent latents into the ball), and v_k the code vector mapped into the ball. Each epoch set g_k=normalize(sum_i 1[a_i=k] A_i). Let P_ab be normalized train transition counts between current first-level regions. Assign a_i=argmax_k{-d_c(z_i,v_k)^2/T + lambda A_i dot g_k + eps D_ik}; use c=1, fixed T, lambda approximately 1 after scale matching, and eps<=0.01 lambda. ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set lambda=0 and eps=0; use the plain baseline squared Euclidean assignment, with ordinary attached model computation (no detached substitute term).

specification.text: Freeze sparse symmetric A, with A_ij the cosine of L2-normalized rows of train-only per-user co-occurrence counts. Let z_i=exp^c_0(h_i), v_k=exp^c_0(e_k), c=1, and d_c be Poincare distance. Let q_ik be frozen directed predecessor-region mass, normalized per item and per code to [0,1]. Choose argmax_k[-d_c(z_i,v_k)^2/T + lambda(A_i dot g_k) + eps q_ik], T=1, lambda=1 after calibrating the median nonzero geometric and symmetric score ranges on the first epoch, and eps=0.01 lambda. objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## The exact mechanism this round must implement

Five earlier iterations in this repository injected the **directed** behaviour structure
(predecessors, successors, transition masses, co-consumption hard negatives) into the
quantiser's assignment. Every one of them lowered the symmetric coherence metric, reproducibly:

| design | largest L1 bucket | `cooccur_overlap_L3` |
|---|---|---|
| plain baseline | ~0.02 | **0.0756** |
| context replaced the assignment | 0.985 | 0.0584 |
| Sinkhorn-balanced assignment | 0.693 | 0.0571 |
| context as an offset on the item latent | 0.166 | 0.0596 |

The only mechanism here that ever *raised* that metric was symmetric by construction: it
grouped items by the cosine of their co-consumption rows (0.0756 -> 0.0786-0.0820). This round
therefore inverts the composition.

**The behaviour signal** is the symmetric train-only co-consumption cosine `A_ij` (every pair of
items inside one user's longest training sequence co-occurs once, rows L2-normalised, the matrix
frozen before training).

**The region profile** of first-level code `k` is `g_k = normalise(mean_{i in k} A_i)`, the mean
co-consumption row of the items the code currently holds, refreshed once per epoch from the
current assignment.

**The assignment** for item `i` is

    k* = argmax_k [ -d_c(z_i, v_k)^2 / T  +  lambda * <A_i, g_k>  +  eps * directed_(i,k) ]

where

* `z_i` is the encoder latent mapped into the Poincare ball (fixed curvature, c = 1) and `d_c` the
  geodesic distance — the curve acts on the same path as the behaviour terms;
* `<A_i, g_k>` is the symmetric co-consumption coherence of the item with the code's region, the
  measured target, with `lambda` about 1 and the two terms scaled to comparable magnitudes;
* `directed_(i,k)` is the predecessor-region mass of item `i` pushed through the train-only
  region transition matrix (the radar of the earlier iterations), and `eps` is at most
  `0.01 * lambda`, so it can only break near-ties and cannot move the partition;
* `T` is a fixed temperature.

## Why this composition

The directed signal is genuinely informative about *sequence* and its own metrics correlate with
recall, but it is not the signal the coherence metric measures: grouping by "who leads into an
item" lowers the symmetric coherence. Putting the symmetric coherence in charge and the directed
signal at a 1% tie-break keeps what the measurement supports and removes what it contradicts.

## Requirements

* the signal and the transition counts are built once from the training split and frozen; no
  validation or test behaviour, no future information;
* `lambda`, `eps`, `T` are source constants; the mechanism must be scale-matched so that one full
  epoch stays near the baseline's 0.15 s on four cards (a 3000-epoch run must finish in well
  under an hour, and the per-epoch work must be vectorised: no per-item Python loops, no per-epoch
  rebuild of the frozen transition pairs);
* the mandatory controls are behaviour-off (the plain squared Euclidean assignment, nothing
  detached), geometry-off (Euclidean distance and Euclidean region means, the curvature removed
  everywhere) and **directed-off** (`eps = 0`, isolating the tie-break);
* report `L1 Hard ER`, `cooccur_overlap_L3` (the target), `adjacency_L3`, the largest first-level
  bucket share, the extension alphabet, and Stage 3 `test_R@10`.

## The gate

The target is the measured strongest: `cooccur_overlap_L3` with a Spearman of 0.902 against
Stage 3 recall over 67 tables, an isotonic out-of-sample R2 of 0.705, a step at 0.0585 and a best
observed value of 0.168. **The arm must clear the plain baseline's 0.0756 before any Stage 3
budget is spent.**

## Frozen constraints

Four tokens, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, no early stopping, the frozen Stage 3 protocol,
baseline `stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_RQ-VAE`.
